1. Calculate the moles of oxalic acid:
   \[
   \text{Moles of oxalic acid} = \frac{5.00 \, \text{g}}{90.04 \, \text{g/mol}} = 0.0555 \, \text{mol}
   \]

2. Calculate the molality of the solution:
   \[
   \text{Molality} = \frac{0.0555 \, \text{mol}}{0.100 \, \text{kg}} = 0.555 \, \text{mol/kg}
   \]

3. Calculate the expected freezing point depression for non-ionized oxalic acid:
   \[
   \Delta T_f = K_f \times \text{molality} = 1.86 \, \text{deg C/mol} \times 0.555 \, \text{mol/kg} = 1.031 \, \text{deg C}
   \]

4. Calculate the van't Hoff factor (i):
   \[
   i = \frac{\text{Observed } \Delta T_f}{\text{Calculated } \Delta T_f} = \frac{1.31}{1.031} = 1.270
   \]

5. Calculate the degree of ionization (α):
   For oxalic acid (H2C2O4), complete ionization results in 3 ions (2 H+ and 1 C2O4^2-).
   \[
   \alpha = \frac{i - 1}{3 - 1} = \frac{1.270 - 1}{2} = 0.135
   \]

6. Calculate the percentage ionization:
   \[
   \text{Percentage ionization} = \alpha \times 100\% = 0.135 \times 100\% = 13.5\%
   \]
